gaps.explanation: can't stand + -ing (also to-infinitive in AmE): can't stand waiting. -ing accepted as standard.

gaps.sentence: When I was a student, I used ___ in shared flats.
gaps.explanation: used TO + infinitive = past habit/state: used to live. (Compare: be used to living.)

gaps.sentence: I remembered ___ the door, so I went back to check.
gaps.explanation: remember + -ing = recall a past action; remember to do = not forget a duty.

gaps.sentence: He's not used to ___ so early.
gaps.explanation: be used TO + -ing: not used to getting (it's a habit he isn't accustomed to).

gaps.sentence: I regret ___ you that the flight has been cancelled.
gaps.explanation: regret + to-infinitive (formal announcements); regret + -ing = be sorry about the past.

gaps.sentence: She forgot ___ the email, so she sent it twice.
gaps.explanation: forget + -ing = lose the memory of a past action (she did send it).

gaps.sentence: On the way to Rome we stopped ___ some photos.
gaps.hint: stop in order to do sth
gaps.explanation: stop to do = pause in order to do; stop doing = finish doing. Here they paused to take photos.
